items.title: Carelon to pay at least $10.35 million in New York settlement over mental health, addiction treatment access - Bee Group Newspapers
items.reason: This item reports a regulatory settlement involving a payer (Carelon) with a state attorney general over access-to-care issues, which falls directly within the payer litigation and enforcement topic.
items.summary: Carelon has agreed to pay at least $10.35 million in a settlement with New York authorities over failures to provide adequate access to mental health and addiction treatment services. The settlement represents a regulatory enforcement action by the state against the payer for access-to-care violations. This outcome affects Carelon's compliance obligations and financial liability in New York and may signal increased state scrutiny of payer practices around behavioral health coverage and network adequacy, matters that revenue-cycle teams track when evaluating claims processing, network management, and denial patterns by payers.

items.title: Molina Healthcare sues over $140M star ratings loss - Modern Healthcare
items.reason: This reports a lawsuit by a payer (Molina Healthcare) involving financial penalties related to CMS star ratings, which falls directly within payer litigation and regulatory enforcement affecting revenue-cycle operations through quality metric enforcement mechanisms.
items.summary: Molina Healthcare has filed a lawsuit concerning a $140 million loss related to CMS star ratings, according to Modern Healthcare. The suit represents a payer's challenge to star-rating-based penalties, which directly impact plan revenue and quality metric compliance obligations. This litigation is relevant to revenue-cycle teams as star ratings drive Medicare Advantage payment adjustments and affect overall payer financial performance, potentially influencing network policies and provider payment negotiations. The case highlights regulatory and financial risks payers face in quality reporting and performance measurement systems that ultimately influence provider reimbursement strategies.

items.title: CMS Set to Recompete Medicare Advantage Audit Analytics as RADV Program Expands - OrangeSlices AI
items.reason: CMS enforcement and audit actions against Medicare Advantage plans (RADV program expansion) directly impact payer compliance, penalties, and revenue-cycle operations for health plans and their provider networks.
items.summary: CMS is recompeting its Medicare Advantage audit analytics contract as the RADV (Risk Adjustment Data Validation) program expands its oversight of MA plans. The RADV program conducts audits to identify and recover improper payments and coding errors, with findings often resulting in penalties and payment adjustments for payers. This expansion signals increased CMS enforcement activity and audit frequency targeting Medicare Advantage plans, which affects how plans manage claims processing, documentation, and provider payment integrity. Revenue-cycle teams managing MA contracts should anticipate more rigorous audit scrutiny and prepare for potential recoupments and compliance demands.
